content:
Maya: trying to get consensus on how we surface "who-won" when multiple routing policies match. Do we log the full decision path or just the final policy id?
Alex: full decision path + chosen flag pls. otherwise debugging is painful.
Raj: agree. but can we keep payload small for high-volume telemetry? need an NDJSON export option that can be sampled.
Emily: +1 to decision path, but we should strip heavy context in sampled streams (no full tenant config blob).
Maya: proposal: two audit tiers - compact (chosen_policy + short reason) and verbose (full candidates + decision scores). Exportable separately.
Alex: sounds good. need API shape though. I imagine something like:
```json
{
  "ts":"2026-03-01T12:00:00Z",
  "actor":"svc-router@prod",
  "action":"route_resolution",
  "tenant":"acct-42",
  "chosen_policy":"p-123",
  "candidates":[{"id":"p-123","score":10},{"id":"p-456","score":8}],
  "reason":"priority_then_latency"
}
```
Raj: prefer adding a tiny trace_id so we can link to console trace. 
Emily: we also need to decide PII handling - tenant id must be pseudonymized in exports for non-admins.
Maya: yes, export modes: admin (full), compliance (pseudonymized), public (compact). document these in export docs.
Alex: console UX question — when viewing a single change in the audit panel, do we show the full decision graph inline or a collapsible "expand decision path"?
Emily: collapsible. default compact so page stays snappy. expand will fetch verbose NDJSON by trace_id.
Raj: API detail — should the route resolver return the chosen policy inline in response to user request? i.e., an opt-in header `X-Route-Decision: trace_id` so apps can record it locally.
Maya: I like opt-in header. It avoids noisy payloads on happy-path but gives correlation signal for customers. document as `X-Route-Trace: <id>`
ops-bot: deployments: canary rollout note — this will require a migration of audit-schema v2 -> consumers must handle `candidates` optional.
Alex: good call. add version field: `audit_schema_version: "2"` on root.
Emily: about exports — we should let customers request NDJSON by time range + schema version + pseudonymization level. do we gate by quota?
Raj: yes. exports are heavy. enforce export quota per-tenant with long-running jobs and pre-signed download links. also emit small job audit events for visibility.
Maya: thinking about retention UI: show last exported time and who requested it in the audit panel. tie to RBAC.
Alex: small sample of an exported line (compact):
```ndjson
{"ts":"2026-03-01T12:00:00Z","actor":"svc-router@prod","action":"route_resolution","tenant_alias":"t-xxxxx","chosen_policy":"p-123","reason":"priority_then_latency","trace_id":"tr-9a8b"}
```
Emily: add `policy_revision` so we know which version of the policy evaluated. avoids confusion when policies change after the fact.
Raj: security question — who can download verbose exports? need enterprise role + export approval workflow for privileged changes.
Maya: agreed. add export approval metadata: `requested_by`, `approved_by`, `approved_at` into the job manifest.
Alex: implementation note: we should avoid storing full verbose events in hot path. write compact into primary stream, async enrich to verbose store when requested or when event marked for retention.
Maya: action items: 1) Alex sketch API + schema v2 draft, 2) Raj design export quota/job flow, 3) Emily console UX mocks for collapsible decision path + export buttons, 4) ops to add migration note to deploy playbook.
Emily: I'll do the UX mock and permission matrix.
Raj: I'll draft export job contract and quota counters.
Alex: I'll open the API PR with schema examples and opt-in header.
ops-bot: created checklist item #2345 for deploy migration and added a note to the canary runbook.
Maya: thanks all. let's sync Thurs 10am if API PR lands before then. If not, push to next sync. :thumbsup:
